A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same bias-learning research. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-classification experiments, bias-versus-mask comparisons, representation analyses, and recurrent-network simulations of oscillators and the Lorenz system.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds scaling, initialization, depth, motor-control and training-time results, including supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The frozen-weight, trainable-bias FNN/RNN procedure is retained. Limited objective changes include the reported learning loss changing from MSE to cross-entropy in Figure 2A and the motor-control adaptation introducing terminal-position, velocity and force penalties in Equation 31.

E1.justification: Section 3.5 adds center-out reaching with a simulated point-mass arm, including generalization to unseen target directions. This substantially extends coverage from classification and signal generation/prediction to motor control. Fashion MNIST was already evaluated in v1, and Nko already appears in its Figure 1C.

E2.justification: V3 adds fully trained networks to the FNN scaling comparison in Figure 1A and directly evaluates their task selectivity in Figure E.3. Representation comparisons add independent-Bernoulli null and mask-versus-mask controls. These extend particular comparisons while retaining the principal fully trained and mask-learning comparator families.

E3.justification: V3 introduces parameter-matched FNN scaling comparisons, Lorenz network-width sweeps and depth experiments. For Figure 2, stated weight initialization changes from uniform to Gaussian, and trained-parameter initialization changes from [-0.1,0.1] to [-0.01,0.01]. Motor-control baseline matching remains inconsistent: Section 3.5 says parameter-matched, whereas Figure E.5 specifies the same architecture.

E4.justification: New analyses test initialization distributions, network depth, task-variance thresholding, active-unit overlap against controls, fully trained task selectivity, and training time. Motor-control experiments also test unseen targets. Conversely, v1's explicit generalization test on 4,320-step Lorenz sequences is absent from v3.

E5.justification: Figure 2 changes its reported run count from four to five and replaces a representative-network variance histogram with a mean and SD across runs. Figure 1A now displays uncertainty shading previously omitted. These refine existing uncertainty-reporting practices rather than introduce a substantially different statistical framework.

E6.justification: Figure 2 reports bias/mask accuracies of 0.934/0.919 instead of 0.915/0.905, and the variance correlation changes from 0.461 to 0.5030. These accompany revised settings and analysis thresholds, so they are not established same-setting improvements. V3 also adds scaling, initialization, depth, motor-control and runtime outcomes, while removing the longer-sequence Lorenz result.

T1.justification: Definition 1 and the FNN results change from integrated L1 error to uniform L-infinity error. The RNN theorem changes from explicitly pointwise trajectory approximation to uniform approximation over initial conditions and input sequences, with a continuous initialization map. Appendix B substantially rewrites Lemmas 1–2 and Proposition 3; v1's auxiliary Lemmas 4–5 are removed.

C1.justification: The central bias-only universal-approximation contribution remains, but its stated guarantee becomes substantially stronger through uniform approximation, replacing v1's pointwise-only RNN qualification. The introduction and discussion also extend the demonstrated applicability claim to motor control.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies v1's functional-specialization interpretation by explaining that task selectivity need not imply task utility. It adds interpretations of parameter-count scaling, discusses mask-learning bounds as worst-case scaling guidance, and explicitly limits conclusions about deep networks. The pointwise-convergence limitation is removed, while finite-horizon and mask-annealing limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix C supplies data counts, batch sizes, learning rates, initialization details, mask-annealing schedules, clustering procedures, simulator equations and stopping criteria; Appendix D reports training times. Much of this was unspecified in v1. V1's promise to release code upon publication disappears without replacement access instructions in v3.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around prefix/prompt adaptation, biological input modulation and motor control, including the new biological-mechanisms table. Appendix B.2 explicitly distinguishes its result from Malach et al. through activation classes, output scaling and approximation targets. References are added and removed, including removal of v1's Petrov et al. citation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, mask-analysis narrative and discussion are substantially rewritten. Related-work ordering changes, autonomous and non-autonomous RNN experiments become separate sections, and the former proof appendices are consolidated into Appendix B alongside new methods and supplementary sections. Terminology changes from FFN to FNN.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2 and 4 are substantially reorganized, with revised axes, panels, legends and uncertainty displays. V3 adds Figure 5, Figures E.1–E.5 and Table 1. The variance scatter moves from Figure 2C to Figure E.4C, while several supplementary scaling panels redisplay results using different axes.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially improves assessment of the central claims through parameter-matched scaling comparisons, overlap controls and threshold analyses, while Appendix C addresses major gaps in experimental documentation. Its qualification of task selectivity also improves interpretive precision. The removed longer-horizon Lorenz test and inconsistent motor-control baseline description are drawbacks, but the stronger empirical controls and reproducibility information provide a clear substantial net benefit.
